back: An interface using windows, icons, menus and controls (buttons, text boxes) operated by pointer, touch or keyboard.
Code runs in response to events (click, key press, form load); each event has its own handler; the user decides the order.
Label: shows text. Text box: typed input. Button: runs code. List/combo box: choose from a list. Check box: on/off. Radio button: one of a group.
An item with properties (data) and methods (actions), e.g. a button with Text and Click.
Property: a value an object has (Text, Width, Visible). Method: an action it performs (Clear, Show, Focus).
A template defining the properties and methods of a type of object; objects are its instances.
Keeping an object's data together with the methods that work on it; other code uses the methods.
A subclass gets the properties and methods of an existing class and adds or changes only what differs.
The same method name behaves differently for objects of different classes.
Convert before arithmetic: Val() in Visual Basic, int() or float() in Python; "3" + "4" gives "34".
